Elaine (People Ops): Hey folks — putting together a super-compact goal-card + manager prompt template for the upcoming quarterly check-ins. Wanted something engineers can paste into self-reviews and managers can skim in 30s. Ideas? :memo:
Sam (Eng Manager): Love that. Here's a 1-paragraph + bullets thing I use. Pasteable: 
```
Objective: Improve inference latency for v2 models by 20%
Why it matters: Reduce user-facing latency to improve retention and reduce infra cost
Primary metric: 95th perc latency (ms) — baseline 420 -> target 336
Signals of success: end-to-end p95 < 350ms in PROD, no >5% error increase, dashboards green
Risks/Deps: model quantization rollout, infra capacity for larger batch sizes
Manager prompt: What help do you need from me this quarter? Any blockers I should remove?
Stretch target: 30% latency reduction or 15% cost drop
```
Jordan (Staff SWE): Nicely concise. One addition — add a 1-line "tradeoffs" field so reviewers see expected quality vs cost tradeoffs. Also a 3-question manager recap at the bottom helps for calibration: 
`Manager recap: (1) FYI on outcome, (2) What surprised us, (3) Suggested next focus`
Claudia (People Ops): This looks great — can we also add a short guideline line about tone for self-reviews? e.g., "be factual, call out help needed, include data points". I'll add a sample checklist we can attach to the template. Also reminder: self-reviews due May 12. :calendar:
Sam (Eng Manager): Agreed on tone. Also I usually ask engineers to include the exact PR/issue links for the biggest wins and one example regression with a blameless summary. Makes calibration meetings 10x faster.
pm-bot: Reminder — Performance cycle window opens in 7 days. See: https://intra.redwood.ai/hr/perf-cycle for timeline and FAQ. :bell:
Elaine (People Ops): Perfect — I'll stitch Sam and Jordan's formats into a single "goal card" doc and drop it in the performance templates page. Final version will include: 1) pasteable goal-card 2) 3-question manager recap 3) tone checklist 4) link examples. Posting in #docs in 2 hrs. Thanks! :sparkles:
